definition: An attention variant (popularized by DeepSeek) that compresses keys and values into a low-rank latent vector, cutting KV cache memory far below GQA while preserving quality.
details: An attention variant (popularized by DeepSeek) that compresses keys and values into a low-rank latent vector, cutting KV cache memory far below GQA while preserving quality. A key enabler of cheap long-context serving.

explainer.lead: Multi-head latent attention is an attention variant, popularized by DeepSeek, that compresses keys and values into a low-rank latent vector. It matters because it cuts KV cache memory far below GQA while preserving quality, enabling cheap long-context serving.

tiers.eli5: Instead of storing a full, detailed note for every past word, the model stores a smaller compressed note that keeps the essentials. That saves a lot of space, so it can handle much longer texts affordably.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers adopt it to shrink KV cache memory well below GQA for long-context serving while preserving quality. It is a key enabler of cheap long-context serving.
tiers.paperLevel: Keys and values are compressed into a low-rank latent vector, reducing KV cache memory far below GQA while preserving quality. Popularized by DeepSeek.

explainer.example: Serving a long-context request, the model keeps compressed latent keys and values instead of full ones, sharply reducing KV cache memory.
